headline: Impeachment Court Sets Two-Strike Rule for Publicity Breaches
seoTitle: Impeachment Court Sets Two-Strike Rule on Publicity Breaches | FMB News
seoDescription: The Senate impeachment court tightened enforcement of Rule 18, setting a reprimand for a first publicity breach and possible fines and speaking restrictions for repeat violations.
deck: Presiding Officer Francis Escudero said repeat violations may draw fines of up to ₱30,000 per offense and restrictions on courtroom participation.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Senate impeachment court announced a two-strike system for enforcing restrictions on public discussion of the merits of Vice President Sara Duterte's pending impeachment case.
Presiding Officer Francis Escudero said the clarified standards will apply prospectively, with earlier statements treated more liberally as the court moves to curb trial by publicity.

sections.heading: How the rule works
paragraphs: Under the system described by Escudero, a first violation carries a severe public reprimand and stern admonition entered into the court record.

For a second and succeeding violation, the court may impose a fine of up to ₱30,000 per offense and, when warranted, restrict an offending lawyer or party from speaking, objecting or examining witnesses on the floor.
Before a penalty is imposed, the alleged violator must receive a written show-cause order and has 24 hours to submit a verified response.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Rule 18 restricts the presiding officer, senator-judges, prosecutors, the impeached official, counsel and witnesses from publicly commenting on matters that go to the merits of a pending impeachment trial.

Escudero said procedural matters and fair, accurate reporting of what happened in court are treated differently from commentary assessing disputed facts, witness credibility, evidence or the likely outcome of the case.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The rule attempts to keep arguments over evidence and witness credibility inside the impeachment court while preserving procedural reporting outside it. It also establishes due-process steps before sanctions are imposed.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Future alleged breaches will test how the court applies the clarified standard, including when it considers fines, speaking restrictions or possible referrals of lawyers for separate professional discipline.
